context_documents.title: 2025-4414 · The rebuild’s full-width intake changes the robot’s supply model
context_documents.body:
# 2025-4414: The rebuild’s full-width intake changes the robot’s supply model

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The interview explicitly identifies this as the second robot and says the original lacked the rebuild’s full-width ground collector. Hollow rollers, compliant star wheels and a floating front feed a polycarbonate funnel and sensor-guided handoff. A continuous internally belted elevator and carbon-tube arm carry a shared pinch claw for coral/algae.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team links hollow rollers to weight reduction and identifies the wide ground collector as a major rebuild objective. It reports testing the star-wheel contact choice rather than presenting it as an arbitrary styling decision.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

The historical lineage should be specific: the team mentions 254’s 2022 hollow-roller construction, while the 2025 task requires orienting rigid coral rather than simply transporting foam cargo. Copying fabrication technique is different from copying an entire intake path. A shared pinch claw can reduce moving mechanisms but its force and retained orientation must remain acceptable for two very different pieces.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test pickup orientation tolerance, failed handoff recovery, and claw retention through rapid arm motion. Keep the original and rebuild capabilities separate in recommendations and comparisons.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.
